Clean-room reconstruction · no MAMMA in the runtime

The Delivered Character

Not a stick figure — the actual skinned character the pipeline exports, rendered from the GLB. Two performers, four cameras, reconstructed by our own geometry. Below it, the per-joint error against the reference solve on the same footage.

Source subject-00/01.glb Rig 55 joints, MPFB mesh Frames 150 @ 30fps Render Blender Workbench
frame 000 / 147
What is missing is as informative as what is there. The hands are rigid — our detector emits no finger landmarks at all, so every finger in that mesh is the rest pose, not capture. The same is true of the ears, which is why the head reads oddly in the joint view: SOMA-77 emits no ear landmarks, and its "nose" is really a head-centre point. Hands cannot be judged from this render, and that is a property of the detector, not the renderer.

Error against the reference solve, per joint

Our triangulated joints against the reference system's fitted joints, on the same 150 frames. Raw is as measured. Offset is each joint's own constant displacement — a definitional difference between where our detector puts a joint and where the body model does. Debiased removes it, and is the closer read on tracking quality.

You spotted the head, and the table agrees. The neck is the worst joint by a wide margin — 91.7 mm median against a 45.2 mm average, with a 247.8 mm p95. But look at its offset column: 74 mm, three times any other joint. Most of it is definitional — the body model's neck is an interior spine joint, ours is a surface point between the shoulders. Debiased it falls to 64.9 mm: still the worst, but the majority of that error is a convention mismatch, not bad tracking.
The wrists and elbows are the best joints on the body — 23.8–25.0 mm debiased, better than the hips or the spine. That is worth knowing before any hand work: the arm chain is tracking well, and what fails at the hands is the absence of finger landmarks, not the arm that carries them.
Three caveats on every number above. The reference is another estimate, not truth — its own fit sits 9–12 mm from its own triangulation, so nothing below about 10 mm is readable here. These are the reconstructed joints; the character you are watching adds another 75–79 mm root-relative on top, because it is a generic body driven by those joints rather than a body fitted to the performer. And the footage and calibration are borrowed — we own no multi-camera footage yet.
Rendered from the run's exported GLBs with Blender Workbench, 50 of 150 frames at every third frame. Errors computed against the reference system's retained pred_joints, subjects assigned by its own labels, on the 14 joints with an unambiguous correspondence.
